SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - NOVEMBER 28, 2022 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

  services agreement with Athens Services pertaining to the implementation of a

  A staff report was given by Mike O’Grady, Utilities Administrator. A PowerPoint

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Tom Voth requested assistance obtaining the agenda report and general information
  about the item.

  Tom Neuberger requested assistance with submission of written correspondence and
  inquired about the contract adjustment amount.

  Kenneth Kung expressed concerns regarding storage and sorting of organics and
  enforcement of the State requirements.

  Gordon Tani inquired as to whether residents could opt to compost all organics and
  avoid a rate increase.

  Murali Vasudevan requested information on the feedback received from the pilot
  program and the City’s upcoming public education campaign.

  Jeffrey Mattison inquired about the City’s public education campaign, potential sharing

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  Jane Dote requested information on the feedback received from the pilot program,
  whether compost bags are allowed, and potential negative impacts of organics
  collection.

  Patricia Alexander provided several suggestions regarding implementation of the
  program in multi-family housing developments.

  Sue Carter expressed support for the minimal increase in rates in order to implement
  the program.

  Michelle Leong stated opposition to any proposed rate increase.

  Bina Bengali stated opposition to any proposed rate increase.

  Jay Gray referenced previous City Council actions related to franchise waste hauling in
  the City and expressed concerns with the timing of consideration of this agenda item.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Carla McKernie expressed concern that Cerritos residents are responsible for paying
  increased costs due to a State mandate.

  David Armiento expressed concern with the proposed rate increase, as it appeared in
  conflict with his Athens billing statement, and that the State should be responsible for
  the increase costs related to the State mandate.

  Gary Clifford, Athens Services, offered to speak with residents regarding the State
  mandate and noted the $10,000 per day fine which could be assessed on the City for
  non-compliance with SB 1383.

  Charles Joslin inquired whether those who already compost at their homes would be
  assessed the fee and if there was an exemption. He also inquired as to the number of
  participants in the pilot program.

  Shaghayegh (Sheri) Meshkinpour expressed support for the program, noting she was
  already separating organics at her residence and was a home composter.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to authorize the Mayor to
  execute Amendment One to the Integrated Solid Waste Management Services
  Agreement with Athens Services and directed the City Attorney to schedule a Closed
  Session for the purpose of discussing the pursuit of litigation related to the unfunded
  State mandated requirement pertaining to the implementation of organic waste
  collection programs (COUNCIL).
